name: Input and TextArea
description: Native text controls with Teal sizing, invalid states, and forwarded refs.

anatomy.description: The native input or textarea element with Teal sizing, focus ring, and a forwarded ref.
A short hint that disappears on entry; never a substitute for a label.
Error styling applied through aria-invalid, either directly or from the surrounding Field.

dos: Set type, inputMode, and autoComplete to match the value, like email or tel.
Wrap the control in a Field so the label and messages stay associated.
Set rows on TextArea to roughly the expected answer length.
donts: Don't use placeholder text as the only label.
Don't disable a field the user must fix; show an error instead.
Don't use free text for a constrained choice; use Select or RadioGroup.

examples.title: States
examples.description: Default, invalid, and disabled inputs share the same sizing and focus treatment.

examples.title: Semantic types
examples.description: type, inputMode, and autoComplete steer the on-screen keyboard and autofill.

examples.title: Search and inline validation
examples.description: Use a compact search control alongside an input that reports its invalid state.

guidance.useWhen: Users enter or search for short text.
guidance.avoidWhen: A constrained set of choices or a long-form editor is clearer.
guidance.behavior: Native input behavior is preserved, including browser validation and refs.
guidance.responsive: Use full width on small screens and constrain width at larger sizes.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to and from the control.
Edits the value using native text editing keys.

notes: Inputs are native elements, so autofill, spellcheck, and input modes work without configuration.
Inside a Field, aria-invalid and aria-describedby are applied automatically when the field has an error or description.
